question: Any patient with hoarseness persisting for more than three weeks requires laryngoscopy to exclude laryngeal malignancy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Hoarseness lasting more than three weeks is the mandatory trigger for laryngoscopy. This threshold exists because early glottic carcinoma is curable, but delayed diagnosis worsens prognosis significantly. Never attribute persistent hoarseness to laryngitis without visualising the cords.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The three-week hoarseness rule is a hard clinical threshold: hoarseness beyond three weeks demands laryngoscopy. In a smoker or drinker, malignancy must be excluded before attributing symptoms to any benign cause.
